original_statement:
Request: Origin: exophial exo-011 (2026-07-18), rule 4 of the sourced design; assigned to aspergillus but never filed there (filed 2026-07-22).

THE RULE: within one match statement (or if/elif chain) dispatching on an Enum-typed subject, two branch bodies whose NORMALIZED AST is identical → WARN 'likely redundant states'.

MOTIVATING DEFECT: would have flagged exophial's PRESERVE/FAIL redundancy (both branches were `Fail(reason)`) — the hand-found malformed-FSM instance that motivated exo-011.

WARN, NOT REJECT — stated plainly per exo-011: textual-identical-body is a decidable PROXY for state redundancy; true behavioral equivalence is undecidable (Rice). Expect false negatives; never promise semantic redundancy detection.

NORMALIZATION: strip locations/comments; do not alpha-rename (keep it a conservative, explainable proxy).

ACCEPTANCE: fixture with two enum cases having AST-identical bodies → WARNED; bodies differing only in comments/whitespace → still WARNED; genuinely different bodies → silent. Non-enum match subjects out of scope.
restatement: This request closes the last unfiled piece of exophial's exo-011 design ('Enforce well-formed FSMs statically', 2026-07-18): rule 4, which was assigned to aspergillus but never actually filed here until 2026-07-22. The rule requires aspergillus's static checker to gain a new WARN-level check: within a single match statement or if/elif chain that dispatches on one Enum-typed subject, if two of its branch bodies have identical normalized ASTs, the checker must emit a warning reading 'likely redundant states'. Normalization here means stripping source locations and comments before comparing — it explicitly does NOT rename variables to a canonical form, so two branches that differ only by variable name are still treated as different and stay silent; this keeps the check a conservative, explainable, textual proxy rather than a claim about real program behavior. This rule exists because textual-identical-body is a decidable stand-in for a genuinely undecidable question (true behavioral equivalence between two branches, per Rice's theorem) — the checker WARNS rather than REJECTS precisely because it will have false negatives and must never be read as proving two states are semantically redundant. The concrete motivating case is real: exophial had a PRESERVE/FAIL branch pair that were both literally `Fail(reason)` — a hand-found malformed-FSM defect this rule would have caught automatically. The rule only applies when the dispatch subject is Enum-typed; dispatch over non-enum subjects (e.g. plain strings or ints) is out of scope even if their branch bodies happen to be identical. The deliverable is one self-contained static check, demonstrated against a fixture collecting several dispatch scenarios, each producing one specific, independently observable warning-count (and, for the core case, exact warning text) when the checker is run over it.

bodies differing only in comments/whitespace → still WARNED
Non-enum match subjects out of scope

goal: Add a WARN-level static check to aspergillus that flags two branch bodies of a single Enum-typed match/if-elif dispatch when their location- and comment-stripped (but not alpha-renamed) ASTs are identical, emitting 'likely redundant states' — catching the exact PRESERVE/FAIL-style redundant-branch defect that motivated exo-011, while staying silent on non-enum dispatch, genuinely different bodies, and bodies that differ only by variable naming.
acceptance_criteria: Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch that do exactly the same thing (like the real PRESERVE/FAIL bug, where both branches just returned Fail(reason)). The checker should flag exactly one warning, worded exactly 'likely redundant states'.

Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch where one branch has an extra comment and different indentation/whitespace, but otherwise does the same thing as the other branch. The checker should still flag exactly one warning.

Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch that use a different local variable name but are otherwise structured the same way. Because the rule deliberately never renames variables to compare bodies, this should NOT be flagged.
Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch that genuinely do different things. The checker should report no warnings at all.

Show the checker a dispatch (match or if/elif) over a plain non-enum value (like a string or number) where two branches happen to do exactly the same thing. Since the subject isn't an Enum, the checker should report no warnings.

acceptance_tests.description: Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch that do exactly the same thing (like the real PRESERVE/FAIL bug, where both branches just returned Fail(reason)). The checker should flag exactly one warning, worded exactly 'likely redundant states'.
acceptance_tests.proves: Proves the core rule: identical-normalized-AST branches over an Enum-typed dispatch are warned, with the exact required wording.

acceptance_tests.description: Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch where one branch has an extra comment and different indentation/whitespace, but otherwise does the same thing as the other branch. The checker should still flag exactly one warning.
acceptance_tests.proves: Proves the normalization step strips comments and whitespace/location noise before comparing, so cosmetic differences alone don't hide a real redundant pair.

acceptance_tests.description: Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch that use a different local variable name but are otherwise structured the same way. Because the rule deliberately never renames variables to compare bodies, this should NOT be flagged.
acceptance_tests.proves: Proves the 'do not alpha-rename' design rule holds: a variable-name-only difference makes the normalized ASTs unequal, so the pair stays silent rather than being force-matched.

acceptance_tests.description: Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch that genuinely do different things. The checker should report no warnings at all.
acceptance_tests.proves: Proves the check doesn't false-positive on branches that are actually different — it only fires on true AST-identical bodies.

acceptance_tests.description: Show the checker a dispatch (match or if/elif) over a plain non-enum value (like a string or number) where two branches happen to do exactly the same thing. Since the subject isn't an Enum, the checker should report no warnings.
acceptance_tests.proves: Proves the rule stays scoped to Enum-typed dispatch subjects and doesn't fire on non-enum dispatch even when branch bodies happen to match.
